hook.line: Mariana asks Tomás what he likes about the neighbourhood. He likes a lot of it, but one thing stands out, and Spanish flags it with two little words.
hook.es: Me gusta el barrio, sobre todo la gente.
hook.en: I like the neighbourhood, especially the people.

examples.es: Me gustan los deportes, sobre todo el fútbol.
Vale cocina muchos postres, sobre todo tortas.
examples.en: Vale makes lots of desserts, especially cakes.

examples.es: Los clientes vienen mucho, sobre todo los sábados.
examples.en: Customers come a lot, especially on Saturdays.

examples.es: Lo hago por mi familia, sobre todo.
examples.en: I'm doing it for my family, above all.

examples.es: Simón grita mucho, sobre todo por la mañana.
examples.en: Simón screams a lot, especially in the morning.

examples.es: Sobre todo, no hables con Altamira.
examples.en: Above all, don't talk to Altamira. (to a friend)

rule:
*Sobre todo* means especially or above all. You make a general statement, then add *sobre todo* and the case that stands out.

*Me gustan los deportes, sobre todo el fútbol.*

It is not a literal "on top of everything". It can also come last, as a short extra: *Lo hago por mi familia, sobre todo.*

Or first, to flag the most important thing: *Sobre todo, no hables con Altamira.*

It is always two words, and it never changes.
smallPrint: Teachers call this an adverbial phrase of emphasis. Written as one word, *sobretodo* is a wrong spelling.

yourTurn.answer: Me gusta el barrio, sobre todo la gente.
yourTurn.why: It is written as two words: *sobre todo*.

pitfalls.wrong: Me gusta el barrio, sobretodo la gente.
pitfalls.right: Me gusta el barrio, sobre todo la gente.
pitfalls.why: Almost. It is two words; *sobretodo* is a wrong spelling.

pitfalls.wrong: Me gustan los deportes, sobre todos el fútbol.
pitfalls.right: Me gustan los deportes, sobre todo el fútbol.
pitfalls.why: Almost. The phrase never changes: *todo* stays singular.

pitfalls.wrong: Me gustan los deportes, sobre todo y el fútbol.
pitfalls.right: Me gustan los deportes, sobre todo el fútbol.
pitfalls.why: Almost. No *y* is needed; the standout case follows straight after.

personal: Say one thing you like about your life here, then add *sobre todo* and the best part.
